infoPlist.NSCalendarsUsageDescription: Portava adds confirmed meetups to your calendar so you never miss a plan.
infoPlist.NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription: Portava adds confirmed meetups to your calendar so you never miss a plan.
infoPlist.NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription: Portava uses your location to show nearby places and auto-publish posts after you leave a spot.
infoPlist.NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescrip: Portava uses your location in the background to track route progress, trigger check-ins, and automatically publish your post after you leave a spot.
infoPlist.NSCameraUsageDescription: Portava uses your camera for video calls and so you can add photos to posts and your passport.
infoPlist.NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription: Portava accesses your photo library so you can upload trip photos and profile pictures.
infoPlist.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Portava uses your microphone for voice and video calls with your travel contacts, and for video content attached to posts.
infoPlist.NSMotionUsageDescription: Portava reads coarse motion on this device to work out how busy a place is. The readings are turned into buckets on your phone and the raw motion never leaves it.

sensingPermissions._comment: Sensing spec §4.1: coarse acoustic energy/rhythm ONLY under separate explicit permission, and §3: collect/retain/aggregate/infer/personalize/surface/share are distinct permissions. Neither iOS nor Android offers a second microphone switch, and Portava's existing one (NSMicrophoneUsageDescription / RECORD_AUDIO) was granted for LiveKit calls and expo-av video. So the separate permission is declared here as its own purpose scope with its own storage key, its own usage string and its own opt-in, and src/lib/sensing/acousticPermission.ts refuses every call/video microphone grant by name. The OS permission is required IN ADDITION, never INSTEAD.

acousticEnergy.usageDescription: Portava can take a coarse loudness and rhythm reading to tell whether a place is lively. It measures a level only — no audio is recorded, kept or sent — and it is off until you turn it on here, separately from the microphone used for calls and video.
